# E4g — what each part is bound by (C1), and what the optimisation changed (C2) (T007)

**Generated by `bench/make_e4g_report.py` from `results/20261025_E4g_c1_summary/`** (the latest C1 directory per model × mode, `bench/t007_c1.py` + `bench/t007_c1_tables.py`). Nothing here is typed in.

**How to read it.** ncu `--set full` plus the 17 warp-stall reasons, tensor-pipe and T003's DRAM / FLOP counters, on **every kernel** of each part (chunked windows; coverage = joined nsys kernel time ÷ the part's nsys kernel time). Every per-part value is weighted by nsys kernel time. Per kernel, the speed-of-light verdict: compute-bound if SM % ≥ 80 and ≥ memory; memory-bound if memory ≥ 80, where memory = max(on-chip memory %, DRAM % of the measured 258.2 GB/s) because this chip exposes no `dram__` counters, so ncu's own memory % omits DRAM; otherwise latency-bound, named by its largest stall; launch-bound if shorter than the part's median launch gap. The part's verdict is the class holding most of its kernel time; the time shares are given. **DRAM GB/s** = ncu bytes ÷ nsys duration; ncu flushes the caches before each replay, so the bytes are cold-L2 bytes and the rate can exceed what the run moves (it exceeds the measured peak where the real run hits in L2).
